records.recommendation: Two distinct regional senses are included in gloss; US-only example and collocations do not demonstrate British washing-up. Add British example (I'll wash up after dinner) or narrow gloss with Master approval.
The Chinese example adds '身上的泥土' absent from English. Fix to '在花园干活后，我想把自己洗干净。'; retain MU-QA REVISE until revised.
The tap is dripping; could you tighten it? is pragmatically ambiguous. Prefer 'The tap keeps dripping. We should get it fixed.' Not a sense-identity error.
Running water itself need not be tap water; '流动的自来水' works for washing hands but narrower than general English expression. Ask Master whether to scope label.
Main English example is tautological ('hot water is very hot'), both flags non-PASS. Replace with 'Be careful—the hot water can burn you' or 'The water is too hot; turn the temperature down.'
Existing usage note accurately distinguishes electric shaver and razor; remaining source gloss breadth can be clarified, but not conclusive material wrong sense.
